unverified.correction:
The recommendation's SPINE survives — KEEP (a), WP3a is a hard publication gate, the hatch is built and must be published honestly, D5's gate and D31's 'blocked on infrastructure' are both stale. Marked unverified because two of the findings offered as §6/§12 normative text are wrong, and one normative claim is over-broad.

(1) RESIDUAL 1 UNDERCOUNTS THE UN-BUMPABLE LANES: FOUR, NOT TWO. Besides `exit_child_pass` (:7097) and `watch_child_pass` (:9898), the SPINE-TIP lane is equally bump-less — `watch_spine_tip_pass` (:1272) / `watch_spine_tip_pass_seen` (:1282) and `exit_spine_tip_pass` (:1341) all call bare `electrum.transaction_broadcast_raw` and take no `BumpCapability`. That matters more than the child gap for point (2).

(2) RESIDUAL 2 IS WRONG IN ITS REASONING AND UNSAFE AS A NORMATIVE STATEMENT. The draft says the TRUC anchor-slot contention 'is NOT triggered by the reference walk' because `exit_pass_ex` 'broadcasts sequentially and BREAKS at the first stuck tier, so the bump is submitted before the successor exists'. The code does not do that: `TierBroadcast::Bumped` pushes and CONTINUES (:10009-10011); only `Stuck` breaks. The root lane is nevertheless safe — but for a different reason, which is the one that belongs in §6: every tier below the trigger carries a positive CSV relative to its parent, so a successor cannot enter the mempool while the bumped parent is unconfirmed, and when the parent confirms the fee child confirms with it. That reason does NOT hold on the spine: `SPINE_CSV = 0` (:6803) and tiers are v3 (lib/src/tesr.rs:410, :708), so consecutive spine tiers legitimately co-exist in the mempool — which is exactly the 'in-flight window of 2, ~68-block stall' WP1 measured (lib/src/tesr.rs:277-278, WP1:119). On that lane a fee child WOULD consume the single TRUC child slot. It cannot happen today only because the spine lane has no bump path — i.e. residuals (1) and (2) are the same hole seen from two sides, and closing (1) opens (2). Rewrite the owner question as: 'may a tier be bumped while an unconfirmed successor exists, and what is the rule on a zero-CSV chain' — not 'is the reference walk's sequential-stop behaviour normative'.

(3) '§12 ... THE MARKET NUMBER IS THE RECEIVER'S OWN ESTIMATOR, NEVER THE COORDINATOR'S' IS OVER-BROAD. True of the Rust client (utils.rs:63-71) and of nodejs (utils.js:11-21, `blockchain.estimatefee`). NOT true of the web client: clients/libs/web/utils.js:8-10 fetches `${clientConfig.esploraServer}/api/fee-estimates` and takes `response.data[3]`, **falling back to 1 sat/vB when the field is absent** (:12-14), feeding web/transfer_receive.js:245. Publish the rule if you like, but say it is a rule the web client does not meet — the same §16 carve-out D4 already needs, plus a fail-OPEN default that D4's carve-out does not have.

(4) THE 180 330-SAT FIGURE IS A KNOB, NOT AN ECONOMICS MEASUREMENT. WP1's run was an isolated node at `-minrelaytxfee=0.00003`, child effective feerate ~567 sat/vB (:66-71); the same note's live rescue reports 'min relay fee not met, **6 < 13**' (:122). DECISIONS.md:583-586 already carries the 900x ratio into a normative argument. Keep it for 'no disinterested stranger will bump a 240-sat anchor', but label it as the configured floor it was measured at, or §12/§15 acquires a protocol constant that is a test flag.

(5) Two housekeeping items for the WP3a commit, since it touches these lines anyway: the module doc at :17130 cites `TesrBundle::fee_rate` as `tesr.rs:84` (it is :253); and GAP C is already CLOSED (:17999-18001, the test now asserts `is_err`), so do not re-list VALUE-CONSERVATION-SWEEP V5's `checked_add` item as open when scoping WP3a — the scope is A and B only.

(6) Minor, but it bites the phrase 'normative width': `fee_rate_tolerance` and `max_fee_rate` are read from a settings file via `get_int(...).unwrap()` (client_config.rs:87, :90; Settings.toml:7, :13), so the DEPLOYED band is integral. The 5.0/1.0 in the draft are the `ClientConfig::new` literals. §12 must either publish an integral width or the config path is non-conformant with its own spec.

The recommendation survives — all three code items are real and correctly scoped — but four edits are required before it reaches the spec.

1. REPLACE THE SEVERITY PARAGRAPH. The draft's own correction is wrong in the unsafe direction. `UtexoInvoice` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, and serde_derive defaults a missing `Option<T>` to `None`. So a one-character typo in an OPTIONAL KEY NAME parses cleanly into a DIFFERENT invoice: corrupting `"expiry_unix"` yields an invoice that never expires; corrupting `"asset_id"` turns a TOKEN invoice into a SATS invoice, and `fulfill_utexo_invoice` (invoice.rs:116-119) then pays `amount` SATOSHIS where `amount` token units were requested — a category error, not an overpay. The correct severity line is: the address is self-checksummed so a typo cannot redirect payment, but ANY single-character corruption of the JSON body — key or value — can silently change the amount, the asset, or the expiry. That is a stronger argument for the checksum than the one the draft makes, and it also means the spec must state absent-vs-null explicitly for all three optional fields (the D9 rule), not merely 'the meaning of every absent optional field'.

2. THE BECH32M PROPOSAL NEEDS A LENGTH CLAUSE. BIP-173/350 impose a 90-character limit on bech32/bech32m strings. A utexo invoice (a ~110-char bech32m address plus amount, asset id and memo) exceeds it by a wide margin. If the spec says 'bech32m under HRP `utexoinv`' without explicitly lifting the 90-char limit the way BOLT11 does, independent implementations using a conformant bech32 decoder will reject every real invoice. Either state the limit as lifted, or take the draft's second option (keep the body, append a checksum under a new prefix) — which is the safer of the two and should be preferred.

3. SOFTEN THE DOCS CLAIM. `docs/utexo/SPEC.md:756-759` is REQ-28, a MUST, not descriptive prose. Accurate statement: no document specifies the WIRE GRAMMAR of either encoding; REQ-28 already mandates round-trip and payer-side expiry rejection (ERR-11). This matters because the draft simultaneously recommends publishing `expiry_unix` as ADVISORY — that is compatible with REQ-28 (which places the obligation on the payer), but the spec must say so explicitly rather than appearing to relax an existing MUST.

4. FIX ONE CITATION: the laddered-split refusal is transfer.rs:1064-1071, not :1130-1138 (which is a comment describing it).

NOTHING REFUTES the three code items. Item 2 (HRP split) is real: `validate_address` (lib.rs:120-127) does only `starts_with` tests, so a signet address passes on a regtest wallet on both the sats and token send paths (`execute_ex`, transfer_sender.rs:979). One narrowing on its consequence language: the draft says this 'can lose real funds today'. A cross-network send does not destroy the coin — the sender's pre-signed backup chain is untouched and the coin remains unilaterally exitable — so the accurate framing is 'an unrecoverable-by-the-recipient send that forces the sender into a unilateral exit', not 'lost funds'. Say the weaker true thing; the case for per-network HRPs does not need the stronger false one.

One flag on scope: the draft sets owner_judgement_required=false, but DECISIONS.md:171 words the coin-type item as 'decide explicitly whether coin type 0 on testnet/signet is deliberate or a defect' — an owner call by construction, and the only one of the three that changes what keys a user's mnemonic yields. Items 1 and 2 are mechanical; item 3 should be put to the owner as a one-line confirmation (SLIP-44 coin type 1 on all test networks), even though D23 makes it free.

The recommendation's SHAPE is right — drop 'retire the absolute deadline', specify three clocks, publish two numbers not one — but four edits are required, one of them to a headline finding.

1. REPLACE THE δ ENFORCEMENT CLAIM. 'δ IS NOT ENFORCED ANYWHERE' is false and would put a wrong fact in §7. The correct split is: δ's VALUE is already receiver-enforced by exact schedule equality (rust/tesr.rs:6580-6625) — that MUST can be written into the spec TODAY and needs no gate. δ's RELATIONAL effect is not enforced: the receiver checks only `sup.csv > live.csv` (rust/tesr.rs:10634-10637) and tier CSVs are range-checked to `[d_floor, d0]` (:10580, :10994) rather than pinned to the `d0 − k·δ` grid. So the sentence 'DO NOT WRITE A δ MUST UNTIL D14 LANDS' must be narrowed to 'do not write the RELATIONAL δ MUST (`sup.csv ≥ live_csv + δ`) until D14 lands'; the schedule-equality MUST and the range MUST are enforced and specifiable now. Also correct 'applied only by the honest builder at next_rival_state_csv' — there are four build sites (:6830, :8013, :8702, :8795).

2. SOFTEN 'STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE' AND WITHDRAW 'NO CODE CHANGE IS REQUIRED'. The property holds on every traced path, but it is produced by three independent filters ([B0]'s F-on-chain test at claim time, the plain loop's carrier exclusion, and `branch-` rows existing only for off-chain sub-coins) rather than by any check. Nothing calls `tesr::load` in that loop and nothing deletes a `branch-` row after materialisation. Write it into §15 as a REQUIRED INVARIANT ('a coin with a ladder MUST have an empty exit branch; a wallet MUST NOT force-exit on a deposit-anchored deadline a coin that holds a ladder'), and add the corresponding assertion to auto_exit_due_inner's plain loop. That is one cheap code change, not zero.

3. DO NOT CITE wallet.rs:2706-2725 AS DECISIVE WITHOUT NOTING IT IS HALF STALE. Its headline ('auto_exit_due is not [the protecting pass]') was made false by D13, which put the ctesr-/spinetip- near-deadline loop inside auto_exit_due_inner (:2137-2144). Its reasoning about the ROOT lane — verifiably-empty branch, genuinely None deadline, 'it would have to invent one' — is still correct and is what the argument actually rests on. Quote that, and flag the comment for repair.

4. RE-PRICE THE TRUC GAP. The draft presents 'window 2, ~68 blocks measured' as the one surviving real gap. That measurement is of the toy schedule on testnet, which D25 retired (lib/src/tesr.rs:263-281 says so in as many words), so a §15 clause citing 68 blocks would describe a configuration the code no longer produces. The surviving, still-true statement is narrower and should be written instead: no term in any budget accounts for relay stalls, and SPINE_CSV = 0 means consecutive spine tiers are exactly the shape TRUC caps at two in flight — so §6 must state the in-flight window of 2 as a NORMATIVE RELAY CONSTRAINT (WP1's own conclusion), and §15 must state that the published margin does not cover relay stalls. Whether to add a term to `auto_exit_margin_blocks_for` should follow a re-measurement on the mainnet schedule, not the retired one.

MINOR: the background loop does not re-enter both passes every poll — `defend_ladders` is gated to once per new block (wallet.rs:1873-1888) while `auto_exit_due` runs every `poll_interval_secs` (:1896-1903). This strengthens rather than weakens the 'at least once per block' recommendation, but the sentence should be accurate. And lib/src/tesr.rs δ line numbers are :256 (mainnet, correct), :261 (regtest, correct), :283-284 (testnet).

EVERYTHING ELSE IN THE RECOMMENDATION STANDS, and the two derivation rules the draft says are the load-bearing unwritten part (bind every CSV to the signed nSequence; read L_k off the signed flat backups) are both confirmed in code and both genuinely unspecified. So is the observation that the default wallet cannot bump (fee_bump: None in both presets).

The direction — option (b), reframed as "specify the design that already shipped" — SURVIVES. Four amendments are required before writing §19.

1. ERR-11 IS NOT MISSING. The claim "skips ERR-11 with no note" is inherited from the roadmap and is FALSE. ERR-11 is defined at docs/utexo/SPEC.md:765, under §13 (invoice expiry), and is normatively referenced at SPEC.md:757 (REQ-28), SPEC.md:807 (traceability) and GRANULARITY-SPEC.md:536/:544 (GRN-ERR-12 = ERR-11). The §11 list skips it because the entry lives with its requirement, not because it was dropped. Delete this from the evidence — it is the weakest item in the draft and it is checkable in one grep.

2. FIX (i) IS A WIRE BREAK ACROSS FIVE CONSUMER SITES, AND IT CONTRADICTS STEP (2). Step (2) says "freeze the two vocabularies that exist ... verbatim"; fix (i) says rename them to snake_case. Both cannot be done. The shipped PascalCase codes are compared as string literals in FIVE places, not the two the draft names: clients/libs/nodejs/transfer_receive.js:372,374; clients/libs/web/transfer_receive.js:169,171; clients/apps/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/mercurylib.kt:3816,3818 (@SerialName); lib/out-kotlin/com/mercurylayer/mercurylib.kt:3816,3818; plus the Rust client's enum deserialization. A snake_case rename silently converts a batch-locked 400 into a refusal on the JS lane (or, with fix (iii) landed, a loud throw) and breaks the Kotlin bindings outright. The draft's own house style argues against it: the wire vocabulary the code actually ships is PascalCase. REPLACE fix (i) with the zero-wire-change version that achieves the stated goal — add #[serde(rename = "StatecoinBatchLockedError")] etc. PINNING the current strings at lib/src/transfer/receiver.rs:30-42, so a future Rust identifier rename cannot move the wire code — then freeze those PascalCase codes in §19. Same property as the cancel lane, no flag day.

3. MISSED DEFECT, AND IT IS THE DRAFT'S OWN ARGUED FAILURE MODE. The generated Kotlin bindings carry only TWO of the three variants: clients/apps/kotlin/src/main/kotlin/mercurylib.kt:3814-3820 and lib/out-kotlin/com/mercurylayer/mercurylib.kt:3814-3820 enumerate STATECOIN_BATCH_LOCKED_ERROR and EXPIRED_BATCH_TIME_ERROR only — TransferCancelledError is absent. A Kotlin client meeting the shipped 410 cannot deserialize the body at all, so the one variant that exists to stop a cancelled payment looking like an idle mailbox is invisible on that profile. So "three client profiles already branch on code" undercounts (4 profiles, 5 sites) and one is already broken against HEAD. Add regenerating the bindings as a fourth pre-publication fix.

4. DEMOTING SPEC.md §11 TO "INFORMATIONAL" HAS AN UNNAMED BLAST RADIUS. ERR-n is the normative target of two other specs' conformance tables: INVALIDATION-SPEC.md:435-443 maps IVL-ERR-1..9 onto ERR-1/2/3/7/12 (and :81, :260, :327 cite them as requirements), and GRANULARITY-SPEC.md:535-536, :544, :571 map GRN-ERR-n onto ERR-8/9/11. Calling §11 informational silently demotes those mappings and SPEC.md:807's traceability rows. §19 must either scope the demotion to the prose STRINGS (keeping the ERR-n identifiers normative as requirement anchors) or explicitly re-point both sibling specs.

Smaller items: (a) types.rs:145-153 UnsupportedVersion is a wire/format error, not "economic/admission" — the blanket characterisation of all 7 SdkError variants is wrong by one. (b) The `?` defect is scoped to the 400 branch ONLY; the 410 branch at clients/libs/rust/src/transfer_receiver.rs:2150-2162 already degrades gracefully via `if let Ok(...)` — "the Rust client deserializes straight into that enum with `?`" overstates the surface. (c) There are THREE assert_not_an_unrelated_refusal helpers (tesr.rs:16295, :16793, :17512), not two. (d) Name a residual tension in §19: lib/src/transfer/cancel.rs:195 documents message() as "The refusal text. Adversarial tests pin these exactly." Publishing "message is NON-NORMATIVE and MAY change in any release" while 82+394 in-repo assertions pin it exactly is a contradiction unless §19 states plainly that in-repo prose assertions are regression guards, not conformance requirements.

(2) THE 'TWELVE' CONFLICTS WITH THE REPO. 'D8's twelve-item enumeration ... six of which are undetectable' is not from DECISIONS.md:168 — it is SPEC-ROADMAP.md:221. The repo's own verify-first enumeration (notes/D8-SIGCOUNT-AUTH.md:47-57) has NINE rows (a–i), of which (a) and (f) are recorded closed in §6/§7 and (i) by D28 — leaving five GRIEF rows plus one 'not a lever'. Pick one enumeration, republish it, and cite it by file.

(3) THE DELETION LIST IS INCOMPLETE, AND THE OMITTED ITEMS ARE THE LOAD-BEARING ONES. DECISIONS.md:168 still reads '**VERIFIED 2026-08-10 — answer is NO, and it is theft-class** ... `response["sig_count"].as_u64().unwrap()` ... Closure = SE-attested counts = enclave work = **excluded scope**, so the spec STATES the assumption; it does not close it', and it points the reader at notes/D8-SIGCOUNT-AUTH.md, whose §1 (:9-14) still opens '**NO. `sig_count` is not authenticated at any hop.**' Both are contradicted by the shipped code and by that note's own §6/§7 addenda. Add DECISIONS.md:168 and notes/D8-SIGCOUNT-AUTH.md:9-14 to the same edit.

(4) THE CONSEQUENCE PARAGRAPH CONTRADICTS THE REPO'S OWN CLASSIFICATION, UNRECONCILED. The draft says the TRUC anchor-slot contention 'is NOT triggered by the reference walk' because `exit_pass_ex` 'broadcasts sequentially and BREAKS at the first stuck tier, so the bump is submitted before the successor exists'. The code does not do that: `TierBroadcast::Bumped` pushes and CONTINUES (:10009-10011); only `Stuck` breaks. The root lane is nevertheless safe — but for a different reason, which is the one that belongs in §6: every tier below the trigger carries a positive CSV relative to its parent, so a successor cannot enter the mempool while the bumped parent is unconfirmed, and when the parent confirms the fee child confirms with it. Five corrections, all to framing rather than to the verified facts.

(1) THE consequence_if_wrong MIS-STATES THE AGGREGATE ATTACK. ladder_binding_precheck requires the SERVED aggregate to actually control the funding output — it tweaks it to P2TR and compares against tx0.output[vout].script_pubkey — so a coordinator cannot serve an arbitrary key and 'let U := D − E_sid pass an attacker-controlled output'. That decomposition is the source's reason the FALLBACK (derive the aggregate from tx0 when the coordinator has none) was rejected — i.e. why the coordinator's record is load-bearing — not what a malicious coordinator does with it. The real residual is exactly two shapes: (a) serve NULL, yielding BindingRefusal::NoCoordinatorAggregate, the only cause a caller may read as 'legitimately no ladder', which downgrades any coin to the un-laddered lane; and (b) serve the true aggregate of a DIFFERENT coin the attacker controls, binding sid X to attacker-controlled F. (2) DECISIONS.md IS NOT AS ONE-SIDED AS CLAIMED. :168 is stale, yes — but the SAME file records the supersession at :227 (D22's row: 'Closure is IN scope — see D8-CLOSE below'), :232 (the D8-CLOSE shape), :268 (D23: 'Require the attestation outright. decisions.correction:
Accept-and-state is right and the corrected closure path is right. Four fixes, one of which changes the cost estimate:

1. THE INJECTIVITY ARGUMENT IS LOOSE AND WOULD BE WRONG FOR A NEIGHBOURING CONSTRUCTION. 'Distinct messages yield distinct challenges, so injectivity is free' is not what makes set membership safe. blinding_factor, client_public_nonce and server_public_nonce are ALL attacker-supplied fields of the conveyed BackupTx, and the recomputed challenge is `H(x(A0 + nh·A1 + b·Q), Q, msg) ± b`. I read the fork to check: the blinding scalar enters BOTH the hash input — blinding_pk = b·Q is folded into fin_nonce BEFORE the challenge hash (session_impl.h:566, :739) — and the additive term afterwards (:749). That circularity is what makes membership unforgeable: solving for a b landing on a recorded challenge is a fixed-point/preimage search. Had the blinding been a pure additive shift over an unblinded nonce, an attacker could set b = h − c and hit any recorded challenge for any forged tx, and the check would be worthless. State the property as 'an attacker cannot produce a fabricated backup whose recomputed challenge lands in the recorded set', with the reason, not as injectivity.

2. 'A DOZEN LINES / CHEAP HARDENING' IS UNDER-PRICED IN ONE SPECIFIC WAY. The blinding and nonce fields are WRITE-ONLY on the >=2 lane today — nothing reads them, therefore nothing tests them — and cosign_tier overwrites coin.public_nonce/blinding_factor per tier (tesr.rs:13840-13843). The recommendation survives — all three code items are real and correctly scoped — but four edits are required before it reaches the spec.

1. REPLACE THE SEVERITY PARAGRAPH. The draft's own correction is wrong in the unsafe direction. `UtexoInvoice` has no `deny_unknown_fields`, and serde_derive defaults a missing `Option<T>` to `None`. So a one-character typo in an OPTIONAL KEY NAME parses cleanly into a DIFFERENT invoice: corrupting `"expiry_unix"` yields an invoice that never expires; corrupting `"asset_id"` turns a TOKEN invoice into a SATS invoice, and `fulfill_utexo_invoice` (invoice.rs:116-119) then pays `amount` SATOSHIS where `amount` token units were requested — a category error, not an overpay. The correct severity line is: the address is self-checksummed so a typo cannot redirect payment, but ANY single-character corruption of the JSON body — key or value — can silently change the amount, the asset, or the expiry. That is a stronger argument for the checksum than the one the draft makes, and it also means the spec must state absent-vs-null explicitly for all three optional fields (the D9 rule), not merely 'the meaning of every absent optional field'.

2. THE BECH32M PROPOSAL NEEDS A LENGTH CLAUSE. BIP-173/350 impose a 90-character limit on bech32/bech32m strings. A utexo invoice (a ~110-char bech32m address plus amount, asset id and memo) exceeds it by a wide margin. If the spec says 'bech32m under HRP `utexoinv`' without explicitly lifting the 90-char limit the way BOLT11 does, independent implementations using a conformant bech32 decoder will reject every real invoice. Either state the limit as lifted, or take the draft's second option (keep the body, append a checksum under a new prefix) — which is the safer of the two and should be preferred.

3. SOFTEN THE DOCS CLAIM. `docs/utexo/SPEC.md:756-759` is REQ-28, a MUST, not descriptive prose. Accurate statement: no document specifies the WIRE GRAMMAR of either encoding; REQ-28 already mandates round-trip and payer-side expiry rejection (ERR-11). The recommendation survives and clauses (i), (iii), (iv) are sound. Three corrections, one of them material.

(1) MATERIAL — THE C-8 CONSEQUENCE IS MISDESCRIBED, and the misdescription is the sentence the roadmap would act on. The draft says a latched coin conveyed with a NULL transfer batch_id 'falls to the 1-hour non-batch rule while its latch runs to 25 h', so 'the published window is a lie in the direction that loses money'. That cannot happen: the CLAIM gate reads the same column the LOCK does. `validate_batch` (server/src/endpoints/transfer_receiver.rs:380-428) obtains the batch via `get_batch_id_and_time_by_statechain_id`, whose SQL is `SELECT batch_id, batch_time FROM statechain_transfer WHERE statechain_id = $1 AND batch_id is not null` (server/src/database/transfer.rs:5-27), and returns `Success` outright when there is no row. So a latched coin with a NULL transfer batch_id has NO 25 h claim window — it has no latch gate at all. The two clocks cannot disagree; they are the same clock. The real consequence of C-8 is worse and different: the latch's all-or-nothing gate (`is_all_coins_unlocked`, and the preimage release it waits on) is bypassed entirely, so the counterparty can claim the coin without the preimage ever landing. Schedule C-8 — but restate its consequence as an LN-atomicity bypass, not a window mismatch, or WP will be written against a failure mode that does not exist.

(2) MATERIAL FOR CLAUSE (ii) AND FOR THE OWNER QUESTION — 'REVERSIBLE FOR ONE HOUR' HAS THE POLARITY BACKWARDS. During the hour the coin is LOCKED: sign/first and sign/second refuse every co-signature, so no unilateral reversal is possible. Unilateral reversal becomes possible AFTER the hour, and then indefinitely, because the claim side has no expiry at all on the non-batch lane (validate_batch returns Success; I grepped transfer_receiver.rs and transfer_receiver.rs's DB module for any NOW()/INTERVAL/expiry and there is none). The honest normative statement is therefore: a conveyed-but-unclaimed transfer is reversible INDEFINITELY — by consent at any time, and unilaterally once the 1-hour sender lockout lapses; the hour is the protection window, not the reversal window. That is a materially more alarming product statement than the draft's, and it sharpens rather than softens owner call (1).

decisions.correction:
The inventory is accurate and the recommendation's direction survives. Six corrections, two of which change the schedule.

(1) OPTION (a) IS MIS-SITED, NOT MERELY UNDER-PRICED — and it is mis-sited on the very lane §8's claim is about. §8's inequality is a RECEIVE-direction claim. The RECEIVE latch's expires_at is stamped by post_paymenthash BEFORE the invoice exists: ssp.rs:625-644 runs create_pre_image → transfer_sender::execute → ln_invoice, and the payer's HTLC arrives later still. At latch-creation time there is no CLTV in existence to compare against, so 'enforce latch_expiry < CLTV deadline at latch creation' is unimplementable on RECEIVE at any price. The only enforceable site is HODL-accept time inside the RLN/SSP component — refuse or cancel a held HTLC whose CLTV deadline is not comfortably beyond the latch expiry. The draft's expansion (carry min_final_cltv through DecodedInvoice) is the PAY-direction half only. §8 needs two mechanisms in two components; price both before scheduling (a).

(2) NEW FAILURE MODE FOR (b)'s PUBLISHED TABLE — THE CLOCKS DO NOT SHARE A ZERO. The latch clock starts at latch creation, the 3600 s invoice horizon starts at invoice creation moments later, the HTLC's CLTV starts at payment. The claim window closes at 3000 − 300 = 2700 s after latch creation while the invoice stays payable for 3600 s, so there is a guaranteed ~900 s tail in which the invoice is payable and the swap is already dead. It fails SAFE (get_preimage gates on the same expires_at, so the SSP cannot settle either and the payer is refunded), but the source comment's arithmetic at lightning_latch.rs:85-86 — '3000 s… ~600 s below the HTLC' — subtracts two numbers with different origins. The published table must give each clock's ORIGIN, not just its length, or it reproduces the same error normatively.

(3) STALE COMMENT INSIDE THE BLOCK BEING REWRITTEN: lightning_latch.rs:202's '// 25h, same window as classic latches' is false — the classic latch is 3000 s, a 30× divergence. It is direct evidence for (b) ('three independent, uncompared constants') and must be fixed with the rewrite.

(4) RATIONALE (ii) IS LANE-SPECIFIC AND §6 MUST SAY SO. The missing expiry gate is on unlock_by_preimage, which serves EXTERNAL-hash latches only. The child lane uses External on PAY (in_ladder_pay's InLadderLatch::External, 90000 s) and ClassicMinted on RECEIVE (3000 s, whose transfer_preimage DOES gate at :141-153). So (ii) covers the PAY-direction child; only (i) — the grace window plus the lock lapsing at expires_at — covers both directions. Stating (ii) as the whole carve-out's justification would repeat §6's current mistake in a new form.

(5) CITE THE CODE'S OWN [F2] AS THE REWRITTEN RATIONALE. tesr.rs:11467-11486 already says: child terminality is not required, the census is made durable by the handover, 'the coordinator's pending-transfer lock… covers the gap between this census and that completion', and 'the verifier must TOLERATE a terminal child — the Lightning-latched lane deliberately keeps one'. The draft's rewritten §6 is that paragraph plus the expiry case. Quoting it makes §6 a citation rather than an invention, and it independently confirms option (d) is structurally available (the receiver does NOT demand a terminal child).

(6) 'RESIDUAL 3 IS STALE' IS HALF RIGHT AND THE WORD IS DANGEROUS. Its MECHANISM description is stale (it cites transfer_sender.rs:60-78 and a hardcoded INTERVAL '1 hour' 'narrowed to batch_time + batch_timeout'; the live query is at :94-102 and uses MAX(latch.expires_at) with batch_time + timeout only as a COALESCE fallback).
